title: On-prem & VPC license tier pilot: per-node fees, support tiers, and upgrade cadence
creator: Amaya Chen
description:
Goal: Validate a repeatable pricing and support packaging model for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) that balances predictable revenue, sales win-rate, and operational overhead. Scope includes: 1) two license pricing pilots (per-node subscription vs. per-GPU tiered subscription), 2) a 3-tier support offering (Standard, Premium, Enterprise) with defined SLAs, and 3) an upgrade cadence policy (security patches, minor releases, major upgrades) and optional paid upgrade service for on-prem customers.

Hypotheses:
- H1: A per-node flat fee with clear device caps will increase sales close rate with mid-market by 10–15% vs current quote-by-GPU approach.
- H2: Offering a paid upgrade-assist service for on-prem will reduce deployment churn and increase initial contract ACV by 8%.
- H3: Explicit, documented upgrade cadence and patch windows will reduce legal/infosec back-and-forth and shorten negotiation cycles by 20%.

Experiment design:
- Pilot segment: 12 targeted enterprise prospects (regulated industries) + 6 current proof-of-concepts. Split into two pricing cohorts: Cohort A (per-node tiers: Small 5 nodes, Medium 20 nodes, Large 50+ nodes) with license fee bands; Cohort B (per-GPU tier: per-GPU price with discounts at volume thresholds). Both cohorts offered Standard/Premium/Enterprise support options.
- Sales enablement: updated pricing sheet, one-pager for each tier, sample contract addendum with upgrade clauses, and an FAQ for security questionnaire responses.
- Measurement window: 6 weeks active trials + 8 weeks contract negotiation tracking.

Pricing sketch (pilot only - illustrative):
- Per-node tier (Cohort A): Small $25k/yr, Medium $95k/yr, Large $220k/yr (includes base support Standard).
- Per-GPU tier (Cohort B): $6k/GPU/yr with 10% discount for >10 GPUs, 20% for >50 GPUs.
- Upgrade-assist service: $12k one-time for on-prem major upgrade support (min 2 engineers, 3-day window).
- Support tiers: Standard (business-hours email, 48h response), Premium (24/7 email + 4h P1 response), Enterprise (named TAM, on-call rotation, quarterly reviews, 2h P1 response).

Contract & security checklist workstream:
- Drafting a short addendum that: fixes upgrade cadence commitments, defines rollback windows for customer upgrades, lists permitted maintenance windows, and documents a standard indemnity and data handling clause for Private deployments.
- Prepare canned answers for top 30 questions from typical enterprise security questionnaires: SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, HSM options, network isolation, audit logs retention, patching cadence, vulnerability disclosure, incident response timeline.

Success metrics (primary):
- Increase in close rate in pilot cohort vs baseline by >=10%
- Average contract size uplift >=8% for customers opting into upgrade-assist
- Reduction in average negotiation time by >=20%
- Positive legal/security signoff template usable in 70% of cases without custom clauses

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Engineering capacity to support upgrade-assist early customers. Mitigation: limit to 2 customers concurrently in pilot, align with ENG-3021 for support ops scheduling.
- Risk: Legal pushback on indemnity language. Mitigation: Legal already engaged; we will use a narrow addendum scope and escalate only for high-risk customers.

Next steps (week-by-week):
- Week 1: Finalize pricing bands & one-pagers, legal draft of addendum, sales briefing (owner: Liam).
- Week 2: Identify pilot customers, enable SAs with FAQ and contract samples, prepare security Q&A pack.
- Weeks 3–8: Run pilots, capture negotiation timelines, collect feedback, legal/security iterates.
- Week 9: Review results, decide scale vs scrap, prepare rollout plan for G2 if successful.

Stakeholders: Product (Amaya/Liam), Sales (EMs + Solutions), Legal (Contracts team), Security/Compliance, Engineering (Private deployment team), Support (SRE/on-call).
